newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT -Dlr eyes upside vs European currencies.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Dlr eyes upside vs European currencies.

text.p: While the dollar is likely to test the upside versus the European currencies on the near term, it shows little stamina to rally against the yen, chartists said on Monday.

"Dollar/yen broke a significant trendline at 119.85, the May 1995 low, and the bias is a little negative is anything. It would take consecutive closes above the 120-yen level to take the pressure off on the downside," said Chris Turner, senior analyst at the consulting firm I.D.E.A.
Turner said there were no clear signal about the dollar/yen trend with 120 looking as a near-term top.
The dollar's sharp retreat late last week was triggered by official comments in Japan seen as hinting the U.S. currency's had risen enough in recent months -- mainly against the yen.
Analysts said how long the impact of such comments would last was key to the dollar's future trend.
"For dollar/yen, it's probably going to be sideways for the time being," Turner also said. "We are not going to see the same losses as on Friday and Monday."
Dollar/yen ended the session in New York on Monday at 119.30/40 -- or about six yen lower than its high on Thursday at 125.35.
Turner said the selloff has allowed the unwinding of long positions and this may augur well for the dollar, mainly against the mark and other European currencies.
"There were some RSI divergences. The market was very long. But a good chunk of that is gone now. So, we are not going to see the same losses," Turner predicted.

"We saw a strong bounce today in dollar/mark. The selloff from 1.7380, the recent high, to 1.6680, the recent low, has very well set the trading range for the next two months," added Turner who also set a range "on the short term, between 1.6950 marks and 1.7120 marks."
Turner found in dollar/Swiss another reason to expect a dollar bounce against the European currencies.

"Dollar/Swiss had a great bounce from 1.41 which confirms the story in dollar/mark," said Turner who equated the drop to the recent low of 1.41 Swiss francs to the fall to 1.6680/1.67 marks. "This means we can expect the dollar to move sideways from here or even a little higher."
Mark/yen also is a cross to watch, analysts said, with 69.40 yen giving clear oversold signals and pointing to an upside likely to top out at 71.40.
